The City-State of Amoni remained neutral in most military conflicts of the time, though they are known to have aided the Achaemenid Empire in war against the Daevites, ~

According to scp-2309, entities who raided Achaemenid are not Daevites, they are Sarkics. It is little bit confusing because Achaemenid called sarkics daeva-generals. Because the word "daeva" originally means "demon" in Zoroastrianism. My friend also misunderstood it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
the Xia culture group saw the rebuilding of Fuxi as an event to be prevented at all costs, since it would free Nüwa

The Mekhanite Empire introduced several important concepts to the Broken Church theology, the most important of which was the idea that it could be rebuilt.

If the Mekhanite Empire first introduced the concept, how did the Xia also know about it? Speaking of, the Xia section should state more clearly they believed Fuxi was a cage that kept Nüwa contained.
Also, you use both BCE and BC.

Other than those issues, I'm glad to finally see the CotBG hub gaining more detail in the same vein as the Sarkicism hub.

item.title: Re: History of the CotBG
item.content:encoded:
I would make the word "Wan" in all caps, since I've seen it more like that.

I wrote "Wan" like that because the information comes from SCP-3391, where it isn't written in all caps.

I would put Yaldabaoth for the Sarkic deity, although I would see why you would just simply not put its name there, since it has multiple names.

I wrote "The Sarkic deity" instead of "Yaldabaoth" because the later didn't originate in the site, but was a reference to the Gnostic demiurge (if the SCP-2510 article, wikipedia and several articles from a Google search aren't lying to me).

I'd also include something near the end about Father Anvil and the Eastern Clockwork Orthodox Church, which worships around 10 deities(I cannot confirm this).

I've only seen Father Anvil and the Eastern Clockwork Church in SCP-2273 and the Heroic Spirit Alexei Belitrov tale, the first of which mentions them in a post-Lifted Veil scenario and the second of which is a crossover RPG card. Since I wrote this assuming a pre-2217 PoV (hence the last sentence, which is blatantly wrong if one reads the article), I can't really include them.
Perhaps I can include a collapsible in the end for post-Lifted Veil information, though I don't know if there's enough articles about it to merit it. It'd basically be "and then the Church was integrated into society and the world didn't end, except in that Aftermath tale, but the Foundation no longer exists on that one anyway".
Anyway, thanks for the critique. I'm not satisfied with the "City-State of Mekhane" name, but I have no idea what would be a better one.
<hr />

item.title: Suggestion
item.content:encoded:
How about adding a "History" tab? I've read all the SCPs listed and there are large discrepancies on how long the Mycenaean Mekhanite Empire lasted, with the 3391 article claiming it was nearing collapse by 1154 BCE and 3777 having them fight the Hebrews on the 1st century CE. There are ways to make them more or less fit, but it'd be preferable to have concrete information on how long it lasted and between what years in the hub.
If whoever's responsible for this page doesn't have the time, I could write it myself. I already have most of the information needed on a file.

Regarding the Maxwellians, I imagine that their gospels are translated into a wide variety of (programming) languages, but is there any particular language that is regarded as "superior" to the others, in terms either of piety or scholarly acumen? Sort of like how Latin was treated in the real world for a long time?

I only had a couple computer programming courses myself, but since Latin serves as a root language for many that came after it (hence Romance languages), I'd imagine the programming language equivalent might serve that role as well. With that in mind, it might be BASIC or C (or C+ perhaps), but again, I don't know as much about programming as I'd like to.
